Run a complete rare disease workup — I have WES and RNA-seq

Microarray Normalization Method Comparison (ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow). Bioc Workflow ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow analog: read raw microarray CEL/IDAT files, normalize with multiple methods (RMA, vsn, lumi, ComBat), compare normalization quality via PCA and variance estimation. For normalization quality comparison and method selection ONLY — NOT for differential expression statistical testing. For differential expression analysis from a normalized microarray count matrix, use nf-core/differentialabundance.

Microarray Normalization Method Comparison (ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow). Bioc Workflow ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow analog: read raw microarray CEL/IDAT files, normalize with multiple methods (RMA, vsn, lumi, ComBat), compare normalization quality via PCA and variance estimation. For normalization quality comparison and method selection ONLY — NOT for differential expression statistical testing. For differential expression analysis from a normalized microarray count matrix, use nf-core/differentialabundance.

Quantify transcripts from RNA-seq reads using Salmon for an rnaseqDTU-style differential transcript usage workflow. | transcript-level quantification from bulk RNA-seq FASTQ reads using Salmon → per-transcript abundance and count estimates

Import Salmon transcript quantifications with tximport and prepare transcript/exon-level count data and annotation for DEXSeq differential transcript usage analysis. | import Salmon transcript-level quantification estimates with tximport and construct DEXSeq-compatible feature counts and sample metadata → DTU analysis-ready count objects

Test differential transcript usage between experimental conditions using DEXSeq on tximport-prepared RNA-seq transcript data. | differential transcript usage testing on transcript/exon-level bulk RNA-seq counts using DEXSeq generalized linear models → gene- and transcript-level DTU statistics and p-values

Apply stageR to DEXSeq differential transcript usage results for stage-wise false-discovery-rate control and report significant genes and transcripts. | stage-wise FDR control for differential transcript usage using stageR on DEXSeq gene- and transcript-level p-values → FDR-controlled significant DTU genes and transcripts

Prepare RNA-seq differential-expression results for integration with epigenomic data. | bulk RNA-seq differential-expression analysis or import of differential-gene results → gene-level log2 fold changes, adjusted p-values, and significant differential gene set for downstream regulatory integration

Process or import ATAC-seq chromatin-accessibility regions for integration with differential gene expression and TF-binding peaks. | ATAC-seq open-chromatin peak calling or import of accessible-region peak files → genomic accessibility regions with differential accessibility statistics for regulatory integration

Process or import ChIP-seq transcription-factor binding peaks for integration with RNA-seq and ATAC-seq. | ChIP-seq transcription-factor binding peak calling or import of TF peak files → enriched TF-bound genomic regions for regulatory integration and peak-to-gene linking

Run fluentGenomics-style integration of RNA-seq differential genes, ATAC-seq accessibility regions, and ChIP-seq TF-binding peaks; link regulatory peaks to genes. | integrative regulatory genomics analysis combining RNA-seq differential genes, ATAC-seq accessibility peaks, and ChIP-seq TF-binding peaks; perform genomic overlap and peak-to-gene association using promoter proximity and/or regulatory-domain linking → candidate TF–peak–gene regulatory relationships and integrated genomic visualizations

RNA-seq + Epigenomic Integration (fluentGenomics). Bioc Workflow `fluentGenomics` analog: integrate RNA-seq differential genes with ATAC-seq accessibility regions and ChIP-seq TF binding peaks, link peaks to genes via + .
Find and rank drug targets for myasthenia gravis

Quantify RNA-seq transcripts with Salmon for an rnaseqDTU-style differential transcript usage workflow. | Salmon transcript quantification from RNA-seq reads using a transcriptome reference → transcript-level abundance and estimated counts

Import Salmon transcript quantifications with tximport for differential transcript usage analysis. | Import Salmon transcript-level quantification files with tximport and transcript-to-gene mapping → transcript-level counts suitable for differential transcript usage testing

Use DEXSeq to test differential transcript usage from the imported transcript quantifications. | DEXSeq differential transcript usage testing on imported transcript-level counts and sample metadata → gene-level screening and transcript-level testing p-values

Apply stageR to the DEXSeq results for FDR-controlled differential transcript usage findings. | stageR stage-wise testing of gene-level screening and transcript-level confirmation p-values → FDR-controlled differential transcript usage results

Implement the Replogle et al. (2022) Perturb-seq workflow for guide assignment from single-cell CRISPR-screen sequencing data, assigning guide identities to cells and producing a cell-by-guide perturbation annotation table. | Perturb-seq guide assignment from single-cell CRISPR-screen reads or feature-barcode output → per-cell CRISPR guide identities, guide confidence metrics, and an annotated cell-by-guide matrix

Perform Perturb-seq hit calling using guide-assigned single-cell expression data, identifying gene perturbations with significant transcriptional effects and reporting hit statistics. | Statistical hit calling for a guide-assigned Perturb-seq single-cell CRISPR screen → perturbation-level effect sizes, significance statistics, multiple-testing-adjusted hits, and target-gene effect summaries

Infer perturbation states and generate an integrated scVI/scANVI embedding for the guide-assigned Perturb-seq dataset, enabling visualization and annotation of transcriptional perturbation programs. | scVI/scANVI latent-variable modeling of guide-assigned Perturb-seq single-cell expression data → batch-corrected latent embedding, neighborhood graph, UMAP visualization, and perturbation-state annotations

Identify and characterize tumor-reactive T-cell populations from scRNA-seq data, including T-cell clustering, phenotype/state annotation, exhaustion and activation signatures, and candidate tumor-reactive T-cell prioritization. | single-cell RNA-seq analysis for T-cell subset clustering and annotation, tumor-reactivity signature scoring, and candidate tumor-reactive T-cell prioritization → annotated cells, marker genes, and ranked reactive T-cell populations

Predict patient-specific tumor neoantigens using somatic tumor variants, HLA alleles, and optionally tumor RNA expression to prioritize expressed high-affinity mutant peptide–MHC candidates. | tumor neoantigen prediction from somatic VCF variants with HLA typing and optional RNA expression evidence → ranked mutant peptide–MHC neoantigen candidates

Assign CRISPR guides to cells in a Perturb-seq screen, using Replogle et al. 2022 as the methodological reference. | CRISPR guide assignment for Perturb-seq using single-cell guide capture data and cell barcodes → per-cell guide and perturbation assignments.

Call perturbation hits from the assigned Perturb-seq cells, following the provided Replogle et al. reference. | CRISPR Perturb-seq hit calling using single-cell expression data and per-cell guide assignments → perturbation effect statistics and significant hits.

Analyze perturbation states using scVI or scANVI embedding after hit calling. | Perturbation-state analysis of single-cell expression data with guide assignments and hit results using scVI or scANVI latent embedding → cell embeddings and perturbation-state summaries.

Identify tumor-reactive T cells in the supplied scRNA-seq data. | Identify tumor-reactive T-cell populations from single-cell RNA-seq expression data using cell annotation and tumor-reactivity signatures → annotated cells and reactivity scores.

Predict tumor neoantigens; obtain the necessary tumor-variant and HLA inputs. | Predict tumor neoantigens from somatic variants and HLA typing, with expression support where available → candidate peptides ranked by predicted HLA binding and related evidence.

Build and run the graph-based pseudotime branch of the single-cell trajectory subworkflow using an AnnData .h5ad input, with R/Monocle3 clustering and root-cell selection, producing annotated AnnData, pseudotime CSV, and trajectory plots. | graph-based pseudotime trajectory inference from processed single-cell AnnData (.h5ad) using Monocle3 → pseudotime-annotated AnnData, per-cell pseudotime table, and trajectory visualization PNG

Build and run the RNA-velocity branch of the single-cell trajectory subworkflow using the same AnnData .h5ad input, applying Python/scVelo with the selected velocity mode and producing velocity-annotated AnnData, CSV summaries, and velocity plots. | RNA velocity estimation from processed single-cell AnnData (.h5ad) using scVelo → velocity-annotated AnnData, per-cell velocity outputs, and embedding/stream visualization PNG
Run RNA-seq analysis and differential expression

Build the graph-based pseudotime branch of Subworkflow Sprint 3 using Monocle3 on the shared AnnData h5ad input, with monocle_cluster and root_cell parameters; produce AnnData, CSV, h5ad and PNG outputs as applicable. | Graph-based single-cell pseudotime inference using Monocle3 in R from an AnnData h5ad input and optional CSV input → trajectory assignments and pseudotime tables, annotated h5ad and plots.

Build the RNA velocity branch of Subworkflow Sprint 3 using scVelo on the shared AnnData h5ad input, with a velocity_mode parameter; produce AnnData, CSV, h5ad and PNG outputs as applicable. | Single-cell RNA velocity inference using scVelo in Python from an AnnData h5ad input and optional CSV input → velocity estimates, annotated h5ad, tables and plots; check for required spliced and unspliced data.

Load and quality-control Illumina EPIC/450K DNA-methylation array IDAT files using minfi. | Illumina EPIC/450K methylation-array IDAT import and initial quality control with minfi → methylation assay object and QC metrics

Perform minfi functional normalization of EPIC/450K methylation-array data. | functional normalization of Illumina EPIC/450K array methylation data using minfi → normalized methylation values and QC diagnostics

Identify differentially methylated CpG sites and regions using DSS on normalized methylation data. | DSS-based differential methylation analysis on normalized array methylation values or bisulfite-sequencing coverage → differentially methylated CpGs and regions with effect sizes and adjusted p-values

Run missMethyl gene-set enrichment on DSS differential-methylation results. | probe-bias-aware gene-set enrichment analysis of differential methylation results using missMethyl → enriched GO pathways and gene sets with adjusted p-values
Run RNA-seq analysis and differential expression
predict CYP450 inhibition and hepatic clearance for new chemical entity

Load EPIC or 450K methylation array IDAT files with minfi and perform functional normalization. | Load methylation array IDAT files with minfi and apply functional normalization → normalized methylation measurements and quality-control outputs.

Apply DSS-based differential methylation testing to the normalized methylation data; support Bismark bisulfite coverage from nf-core/methylseq as an alternative input where applicable. | DSS differential methylation testing on compatible normalized array methylation data or Bismark bisulfite coverage → differential methylation results for downstream enrichment.

Perform missMethyl gene-set enrichment using the differential methylation results. | Gene-set enrichment of differential methylation results using missMethyl → enriched gene sets and associated statistics.

Nanostring GeoMx DSP Analysis (GeoMxWorkflows). Bioc Workflow `GeoMxWorkflows` analog: read Nanostring GeoMx DSP NanoStringGeoMxSet, segment-level QC, Q3 normalization, mixed-model linear DE across regions of interest.

Predict CYP450 inhibition for a new chemical entity; request its molecular structure and relevant CYP isoforms. | Predict CYP450 isoform inhibition from a molecular structure or SMILES → isoform-specific inhibition predictions.

Predict hepatic clearance for the new chemical entity; request its molecular structure and any relevant species or experimental parameters. | Predict hepatic clearance from a molecular structure and available pharmacokinetic parameters → estimated hepatic clearance with stated assumptions.

Nanostring GeoMx DSP Analysis (GeoMxWorkflows). Bioc Workflow `GeoMxWorkflows` analog: read Nanostring GeoMx DSP NanoStringGeoMxSet, segment-level QC, Q3 normalization, mixed-model linear DE across regions of interest.

Illumina 450k/EPIC Methylation Array DMR Analysis (methylationArrayAnalysis). Bioc Workflow `methylationArrayAnalysis` analog: read IDAT files via minfi, QC, normalize (SWAN or noob), call DMPs (limma), DMRs (DMRcate), gene-set test (missMethyl).

Illumina 450k/EPIC Methylation Array DMR Analysis (methylationArrayAnalysis). Bioc Workflow `methylationArrayAnalysis` analog: read IDAT files via minfi, QC, normalize (SWAN or noob), call DMPs (limma), DMRs (DMRcate), gene-set test (missMethyl).
FDA Phase II to Phase III dose justification brief

Public RNA-seq Reanalysis (recountWorkflow). Bioc Workflow `recountWorkflow` analog: pull uniformly-processed counts from recount2/3 for a study (e.g., SRP), scale counts by read length, run DESeq2 DE with technical replicate handling.

Estimate human pharmacokinetic parameters from rat, mouse, or dog preclinical PK data using interspecies scaling for first-in-human projection. | allometric interspecies scaling of preclinical animal pharmacokinetic parameters (rat, mouse, and/or dog) to predict human clearance, volume, half-life, and initial human PK parameters → human PK parameter estimates for PBPK model parameterization

Run a mechanistic human PBPK compartmental simulation using scaled human PK parameters, including organ-specific clearance and optional renal or hepatic impairment submodels for special-population dosing. | mechanistic whole-body human physiologically based pharmacokinetic simulation using compartmental distribution and organ-specific hepatic and renal clearance, with optional renal-impairment and hepatic-impairment population models → concentration-time profiles, exposure metrics, and special-population dose-adjustment scenarios

Perform Monte Carlo PBPK simulations to characterize interindividual variability in human and renal/hepatic impairment populations and report exposure distributions for regulatory dose-projection packages. | Monte Carlo simulation of a mechanistic human PBPK model across virtual healthy and special-population cohorts → distributions of AUC, Cmax, clearance, variability intervals, probability of target-exposure attainment, and dose-adjustment support

Process RNA-seq data to generate a differential-expression transcriptional signature for subsequent drug-signature matching. | RNA-seq processing and differential gene-expression analysis from bulk or single-cell sequencing input → ranked upregulated and downregulated gene signature

Query drugs with transcriptional signatures matching the RNA-seq-derived gene-expression signature, prioritizing compounds and mechanisms of action. | drug perturbation signature matching using a ranked RNA-seq differential-expression gene signature against LINCS/Connectivity Map profiles → ranked candidate drugs and mechanisms of action

Public RNA-seq Reanalysis (recountWorkflow). Bioc Workflow `recountWorkflow` analog: pull uniformly-processed counts from recount2/3 for a study (e.g., SRP), scale counts by read length, run DESeq2 DE with technical replicate handling.

Estimate human PK parameters and support first-in-human dose projection from rat, mouse, or dog preclinical data using species scaling. | Allometric interspecies scaling of preclinical animal pharmacokinetic parameters from per-species tabular measurements → estimated human clearance and other supported PK parameters.

Run mechanistic human PBPK simulation with organ-specific clearance using the scaled PK estimates, optionally including renal or hepatic impairment for special-population dosing. | Mechanistic compartmental PBPK simulation using scaled PK estimates and compound-specific physiological and clearance parameters, with optional renal or hepatic impairment submodels → concentration-time profiles and exposure estimates.

Use Monte Carlo sampling of the PBPK model to characterize pharmacokinetic variability. | Monte Carlo sampling of specified PBPK model parameter distributions → population concentration-time profiles, exposure distributions, and variability summaries.

Analyze RNA-seq data to generate a transcriptional signature for drug matching. | RNA-seq expression analysis from the available input format to produce a gene-level transcriptional signature for downstream drug comparison

Find drugs whose transcriptional signatures match the RNA-seq-derived signature. | Compare an RNA-seq-derived gene expression signature against reference drug perturbation signatures and rank drugs by signature similarity

Run Voyager spatial ESDA on this Visium dataset

Validate an input population pharmacokinetic dataset for NONMEM-compatible structure, including required ID, TIME, DV, dosing/event, covariate, missing-value, and unit consistency checks. | population pharmacokinetic dataset validation for NONMEM/nlmixr2 modeling using a tabular concentration-time dataset → validated analysis dataset and structured QC report

Generate a NONMEM control stream for PopPK estimation, execute it with nmfe75/nmfe74 when NONMEM_HOME and NONMEM_LICENSE_FILE are available, and otherwise fit the equivalent model using nlmixr2 in R. | conditional population pharmacokinetic model estimation from a validated tabular concentration-time dataset: generate NONMEM control stream, execute NONMEM when a BYOL installation and license are configured, otherwise run an equivalent nlmixr2 R model → parameter estimates, diagnostics, and execution provenance

Phase A — configure an ICH S7A core battery safety pharmacology simulation for the test compound, including exposure range, species/model assumptions, and study endpoints. | safety pharmacology simulation setup for a test compound — define concentration/dose scenarios, pharmacokinetic exposure assumptions, and CNS, respiratory, and cardiovascular endpoint plan

Phase B — simulate cardiovascular safety pharmacology outcomes, including cardiac ion-channel liability, ECG/QT-related risk, heart rate, blood pressure, and hemodynamic effects. | cardiovascular safety pharmacology simulation for a test compound — ion-channel and QT-risk assessment with simulated heart-rate, blood-pressure, ECG, and hemodynamic endpoints

Phase C — simulate central nervous system and respiratory safety pharmacology outcomes, including behavioral, motor, sedation, seizure-risk, respiratory rate, and oxygenation endpoints. | CNS and respiratory safety pharmacology simulation for a test compound — simulated neurobehavioral, motor-function, sedation, seizure-liability, respiratory-rate, and oxygenation endpoints

Phase D — integrate cardiovascular, CNS, and respiratory simulation results into an ICH S7A core battery safety pharmacology report with risk classification and follow-up recommendations. | integrated ICH S7A core battery safety pharmacology assessment — combine cardiovascular, CNS, and respiratory simulation results into a safety-risk matrix and decision-ready report

Phase A: Simulate cardiovascular safety pharmacology endpoints for the ICH S7A core battery. | Cardiovascular safety pharmacology simulation using compound and model inputs → predicted cardiovascular endpoint results

Phase B: Simulate central nervous system safety pharmacology endpoints for the ICH S7A core battery. | Central nervous system safety pharmacology simulation using compound and model inputs → predicted CNS endpoint results

Phase C: Simulate respiratory safety pharmacology endpoints for the ICH S7A core battery. | Respiratory safety pharmacology simulation using compound and model inputs → predicted respiratory endpoint results

Phase D: Integrate the simulated cardiovascular, CNS, and respiratory results into an ICH S7A core battery summary. | Integrate simulated safety pharmacology endpoint tables across three organ systems → consolidated results and model-limitations report

Validate the NONMEM-format PopPK dataset structure, including ID, TIME and DV columns. | Validate a NONMEM-format population pharmacokinetic dataset for required columns and structure → validation report and validated dataset

Generate the NONMEM control configuration using NONMEM_CTL_GENERATE; the supplied step description ends at 'Generate NO'. | Generate a NONMEM population pharmacokinetic control configuration from a validated dataset and specified model parameters → NONMEM control stream

Estimate the population pharmacokinetic model using NONMEM nmfe75 or nmfe74 when NONMEM_HOME and NONMEM_LICENSE_FILE are set; otherwise use the nlmixr2 R fallback. | Estimate a population pharmacokinetic model from a validated NONMEM-format dataset using licensed NONMEM or an equivalent nlmixr2 model → parameter estimates and fit diagnostics

Validate a molecular SMILES input file containing one SMILES string and compound ID per line; report invalid structures, duplicate identifiers, and standardized valid records. | SMILES file validation and molecular structure standardization for a line-delimited SMILES-plus-identifier dataset → validated standardized molecule table and QC report

Perform RDKit RECAP decomposition of validated molecules into scaffolds and associated R-group fragments. | RECAP-based molecular fragmentation of validated SMILES structures using RDKit → scaffold cores, R-groups, and molecule-to-fragment mapping table

Use mmpdb to construct matched molecular pairs from decomposed molecules and estimate property deltas associated with fragment substitutions. | matched molecular pair analysis using mmpdb on a standardized molecular dataset → fragment-transformation rules, matched-pair statistics, and property-delta estimates for substitutions

Rank novel scaffold and fragment-swap candidates by observed transformation frequency, drug-likeness, and synthetic accessibility score. | cheminformatics prioritization of molecular scaffold or fragment-swap candidates using transformation frequency, drug-likeness descriptors, and synthetic accessibility scoring → ranked candidate table with component scores

Validate an expression matrix and matched clinical metadata before differential-expression and gene-signature analysis. | quality validation and harmonization of a bulk gene-expression count matrix with sample-level clinical metadata → validated matrix, metadata, sample matching report, and covariate-ready design table

Perform covariate-adjusted differential expression using voom transformation, limma linear modeling, empirical-Bayes moderation, and topTable output including logFC and adjusted P values. | differential gene expression on a bulk RNA-seq gene count matrix using limma-voom with clinical covariates → per-gene log fold change, moderated statistics, and Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted P values

Score samples with GSVA or ssGSEA using the 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets and identify pathways most enriched in each group. | gene-set signature scoring on a normalized bulk gene-expression matrix using GSVA/ssGSEA with the 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets → per-sample pathway scores and group-wise enriched pathway rankings

Validate a SMILES input file containing one SMILES and compound ID per line. | Validate molecular structures and identifiers from a SMILES-plus-ID file → validated molecules and an invalid-record report.
Use RDKit RECAP to decompose the validated molecules into scaffolds and R-groups. | RECAP decomposition of validated SMILES using RDKit → molecular scaffolds and associated fragments.

Use mmpdb to identify matched molecular pair fragment swaps and calculate property deltas. | Matched molecular pair analysis using mmpdb on validated molecular structures and compound property values → fragment transformations and property deltas.

Rank novel scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness, and synthetic accessibility score. | Rank molecular scaffolds from matched-pair and decomposition results by occurrence frequency, drug-likeness, and synthetic accessibility → ranked scaffold report.

Validate the discovery expression matrix and clinical metadata for the requested analysis. | Validate a gene expression matrix and sample metadata table for sample matching, identifiers, missing values, and suitability for voom → validated inputs and QC report.

Apply voom and a covariate-adjusted limma linear model with eBayes and topTable to the validated discovery data; report logFC and adjusted p-values. | Differential gene expression using limma-voom on a suitable raw gene count matrix and sample metadata, with covariate-adjusted linear modeling and empirical Bayes → topTable with log fold changes and adjusted p-values.

Score the 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets with GSVA or ssGSEA and report the top enriched pathways per group. | Gene-set signature scoring on an expression matrix using GSVA or ssGSEA with MSigDB Hallmark gene sets, followed by group-level pathway summaries → sample-by-pathway scores and top pathways per group.
